name: Naturpark Zillertaler Alpen
kurzbeschreibung: The High Alps Nature Park Zillertaler Alpen protects an untamed wilderness of glaciers and peaks around the mountaineering village of Ginzling and the Berlin High Trail.
preis: Free access (toll roads into tributary valleys charge fees)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; alpine trekking recommended June to October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The High Alps Nature Park Zillertaler Alpen encompasses 422 square kilometres in the upper Zillertal valley, spanning elevations from 1,000 metres up to the glaciated summit of the Hochfeiler (3,511 m) along the South Tyrolean border. Designated as a tranquil preservation zone, the park intentionally avoids mechanical ski lift infrastructure, safeguarding one of the most pristine high-alpine wilderness regions in the Eastern Alps. Colossal glaciers, roaring meltwater torrents, sapphire tarns, and sheer granite-gneiss walls dominate deep glacial valleys including the Zemmgrund, Stilluptal, Zillergrund, and Tuxertal. The idyllic mountaineering village of Ginzling serves as the geographical heart and welcoming gateway to this protected sanctuary.

Route & Anforderungen

Hiking routes within the nature park are legendary, catering to day hikers seeking scenic huts as well as ambitious mountaineers undertaking multi-day high-altitude treks. Chief among these is the renowned Berlin High Trail (Berliner Höhenweg), a demanding hut-to-hut trek traversing the core of the glacier-clad range. A premier day excursion ascends from Ginzling through the dramatic Zemmgrund to the heritage-listed Berliner Hütte (2,042 m), celebrated as the most opulent historic Alpine Club refuge in Tyrol. While lower valley trails are straightforward for walkers with basic fitness, high-altitude passes and summit ascents necessitate surefootedness, a head for heights, and full alpine equipment.

Besuch & Anreise

The principal gateway is Mayrhofen in the upper Zillertal, from which roads lead south toward Ginzling and the secluded mountain valleys. Ginzling hosts the modern nature park centre featuring the captivating 'Hidden Treasures' mineral exhibition. During the hiking season, scheduled hiker buses run from Mayrhofen through Ginzling to remote trailheads and reservoirs like Schlegeis and Zillergründl, facilitating sustainable car-free excursions.

Tipps

Do not miss exploring the historic Berliner Hütte to marvel at its magnificent five-metre-high timber-paneled dining salon dating from the late 19th century. Inside the Naturparkhaus in Ginzling, the sparkling mineral exhibit showcases world-famous Zillertal garnets and quartz crystals found by local mountain prospectors.
